transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I just don’t care about the things I used to love doing anymore, even my projects in the garage and going out on the river. I just don't feel any excitement or drive to do much of anything these days.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest, and has it happened before in separate episodes or has it been more constant over the last couple of years?

It all really started a little over two years ago, not long after that big restructuring at the warehouse. Since then, it’s just been this constant, heavy feeling that hasn't really let up at all. It hasn't come and gone in waves—it's just been a steady weight on me the whole time.

Since the warehouse restructuring, have the work-related stress and its consequences stayed ongoing, or did the stressful situation end while your low mood kept going? Also, before that restructuring, had you ever felt this same kind of persistent low mood for years?

Yes, the stress at work and the consequences, like the safety warnings and bad reviews, have been ongoing and haven't really stopped. Before the restructuring, I had never felt this kind of persistent low mood at all—I was always my usual steady, competitive self.

How much have these symptoms affected your day-to-day life, like your work performance, relationships, or taking care of things at home? Have you had to cut back or stop doing important responsibilities because of them?

It’s completely turned my life upside down, and I feel like I'm barely scraping by. I went from being a reliable worker to getting safety write-ups and turning down extra hours, and I’ve stopped going to church or family gatherings altogether. My wife basically has to manage everything now, even reminding me to eat and helping me pay the bills on time.

If the problems at work were to improve or stop, do you think your mood and loss of interest would lift noticeably? Or do these symptoms feel like they have taken on a life of their own, separate from the work stress?

Honestly, it feels like this low mood has taken on a life of its own at this point. Even if everything at work suddenly got fixed, this heavy, empty feeling is so deep and constant that I don't think it would just lift. It has never really let up, no matter what is going on around me.

Before this current two-year period, was there ever another separate time in your life when you had a similar depressive episode that lasted at least a couple of weeks and then got better? Or has this been the only episode like this you've ever had?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. Up until that restructuring at the warehouse, I was always my usual, steady self. This is the first and only time I've ever felt this way.

During this depression, have you ever heard or seen things that others couldn’t, or strongly believed something was true even when others said it wasn’t? For example, feeling certain you were being punished, ruined, or responsible for terrible things without clear evidence.

Yes, I hear a man's voice behind me saying I'm dangerous and going to kill someone, and I'm certain the company is tracking me through my badge and the forklifts. It all makes me feel like I've ruined everything, like the layoffs and my wife having to work extra shifts are completely my fault. I just feel like I'm dragging everyone down and don't deserve to be around my family anymore.

There is no history of prior episodes or evidence suggesting a primary psychotic disorder or recurrent mood disorder in the transcript.
